# 2026-11-24 Detail

**Period:** 2026-10-25–2026-11-24
**Repository baseline:** `69929a45c1878d22830b3417279c631ab69a883c` (exclusive; dated 2026-10-24)
**End commit on `main`:** `db8c80a424b8833dc169a838e846b0c002d59ffe` (inclusive)

This period focused on billing reliability, Kubernetes deployment preparation, and API and tooling improvements. Local billing UAT covered several payment flows but left high-risk cases open; homelab deployment has not yet been verified end to end.

Repository evidence is limited to what landed on `main` in the commit range; pending PRs are referenced only as future work. A few commits in the range are dated 24 October. The billing UAT workbook and progress log are supplemental evidence published separately, and the homelab status includes information supplied by the project owner. The AI backend work merged in `6edb58723852` is excluded because it was reported earlier.

## 1. Billing reliability and contracts

### Domain and transaction improvements

* Refactored billing domain models and value objects, including money, payment, price, subscription, and refund-related types. The changes clarify ownership and invariants and reduce accidental mutation. Further cleanup removed unused contact-update behavior. See [#365](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/365), `d78e47a3`, and `709bd76e`.
* Introduced a **transactional outbox**: billing database writes and outgoing events are persisted in the same transaction, then forwarded asynchronously. Provider cancellation and refund submission are driven by outbox events. This reduces the risk of a committed state change without a corresponding event; it does not remove the need for retries and idempotency. See `d78e47a3` and the [billing documentation](/services/billing/).
* Improved duplicate checkout handling under a workspace account lock and refund settlement handling, including not reopening settled refunds. Added or updated tests around billing domain behavior, provider interactions, and webhooks (`d78e47a3`).
* Made billing features and limits explicit types across the contract and dependent services, rather than relying solely on generic string keys (`f758ec9c`, `18cca64c`).
* Fixed Stripe customer-portal catalog configuration by specifying allowed update fields (`5196957d`), and improved sandbox customer descriptions (`775223ce`).

### API improvements

* Changed `GET /billing/workspaces/{workspaceId}/subscription` to `GET /billing/workspaces/{workspaceId}` because the response contains both subscription and payer, either of which may be null. Updated nullable response fields and required-field declarations (`a780d8bb`). This is a route change for API consumers.
* Expanded examples for plans, free workspace entitlements, and billing responses and clarified operation descriptions and webhook tagging (`ec85c290`, `a60d17ec`, `9e01d768`, `f6d2060c`, `2add6fca`).

### Manual Stripe sandbox UAT

Manual testing was performed through Scalar and a Stripe sandbox. The [billing UAT workbook and progress log](https://gist.github.com/KevinNitroG/c777cd1c79d017c3ae9122fde8ebb753) are published separately on GitHub Gist, not committed as report attachments. A complete billing UI was not available for this test; results do **not** establish an end-user UI flow or production readiness.

| Scenario                                                                  | Recorded result                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Catalog and free workspace                                                | Pass: expected plans and free entitlements observed.                                                                                                                |
| Plus monthly checkout                                                     | Pass: payment, active subscription, payer, and Plus entitlements observed.                                                                                          |
| Immediate cancellation and refund                                         | Pass for the observed cancellation and refund behavior.                                                                                                             |
| Plus monthly to Pro lifetime                                              | Pass: Stripe confirmed cancellation and refund of the old subscription. Direct lifetime purchase from a free workspace was not tested.                              |
| Another recurring purchase; plan change; cancellation at period end       | Partial, not full passes.                                                                                                                                           |
| Declined initial payment                                                  | Partial; post-attempt entitlements response outstanding.                                                                                                            |
| Lifetime cancellation                                                     | Local cancellation, free entitlements, and a successful refund were recorded; Stripe Dashboard confirmation and the outside-window variation remain outstanding.    |
| Replayed webhook                                                          | Partial: a locally signed replay returned 204 and produced no duplicate local refund or subscription; full Stripe-side and API acceptance checks were not repeated. |
| Admin access                                                              | Admin reads and non-admin rejection observed; status capture and update/invalid-input cases incomplete.                                                             |
| Direct yearly purchase                                                    | Skipped.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Duplicate checkout, permission boundaries, delivery interruption/recovery | Deferred, blocked, or not tested; permission testing lacked a second workspace user.                                                                                |

The record notes one transient local DNS-related webhook delivery failure; the cause was not established. It also identifies sensitive headers, cookies, webhook payloads, and other sensitive data in logs, with a token exposed in diagnostic output. **Follow up by revoking the affected session/token and fixing sensitive logging**; the notes do not establish that this has already happened.

## 2. Kubernetes, Helm, and homelab

### Implemented

* Added a shared Helm library and service charts for web, note, authorization, billing, document, and search-worker, plus an authenticated edge. A chart for the existing AI service was included in later deployment work. Charts include service-specific values, schemas, workload/service resources, optional autoscaling and disruption controls, migration or seed hooks where applicable, and automated chart checks. See [#370](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/370) (`72beeadf`) and [#379](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/379) (`8c90e9bb`).
* Prepared applications for deployment: separated migration and mandatory-data initialization commands, added or improved health/readiness behavior, and adjusted deployment-related configuration. Search-worker readiness accounts for Kafka connectivity; document includes dependency readiness and a migration runner.
* Prepared Flux-based homelab GitOps wiring for releases and infrastructure, including databases, Meilisearch, Valkey instances, and encrypted secret manifests ([#376](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/376), `3af652e4`). Upgraded the **Valkey Helm chart** to `1.0.0` (`46201ed2`); this refers to the chart version, not a claim that the Valkey server is version 1.0.0.
* Added Kubernetes CI and service-release automation, chart version checks, release tag scripts, and an initial development release (`8c90e9bb`, `a97d424b`). Improved test reporting and reduced duplicate CI runs (`c97d3dad`, `d1aaf760`, `7766cc6d`).
* Prepared additional homelab values and secrets, plus RustFS and Stripe webhook setup documentation (`6e9f301f`, `4522f0b6`). Not all inputs are filled.

### Still in progress / deployment gates

The project owner reports that homelab secrets and environment values are being populated and RustFS is being configured. The application has **not yet been deployed and verified end to end** on the homelab.

Before treating the deployment as ready, the [documented Kubernetes limitations](/developer/limitations/kubernetes-deployment) call for live verification of identity-header boundaries and direct-access prevention, authorization policy seeding and safe recovery, image permissions and filesystems, health and routing, and upgrades. Document replica event delivery also has [known limitations](/developer/limitations/document-replica-events). Rendered charts and unit tests are useful but cannot prove these live-cluster properties.

## 3. API correctness and developer authentication

* In `234f7efa`, introduced separate creation request schemas for folders, notes, and workspaces instead of reusing full resource/response schemas. The latter include server-generated, read-only fields that may be required in responses but should not be required from clients. The note API was **already OpenAPI 3.1.2** before this commit; this was a contract correction for 3.1 validation, not an upgrade from 3.0 to 3.1 in this reporting range.
* OpenAPI 3.1 treats `readOnly` as a JSON Schema annotation and discusses applying `required` in the relevant request/response context; tooling can interpret this differently. Separate schemas make the input contract explicit and avoid relying on validator-specific behavior. Reference: [OpenAPI 3.1.2 Schema Object: `readOnly` and `writeOnly`](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.2.html#extended-validation-with-readonly-and-writeonly).
* Enabled local Authentik fixture users and the API viewer client for password-grant testing (`a115e9d0`), complementing authorization-code and refresh-token configuration (`aba81097`). These fixture credentials and password grants are for local development; do not generalize them to production use.
* Expanded OAuth default scopes for API exploration (`17cc93ac`). Updated Redocly CLI to `2.82.0` (`2e80d890`); the update did not require application code changes.

## 4. Toolchains, dependencies, and build quality

* Split mise into shared, dev, and CI environments and added per-environment lockfiles (`711a6384`, `201943ad`). The split avoids installing local-only tools in CI and vice versa; locked versions, checksums, and dependency graphs support repeatable installations across machines. See [mise tooling](/developer/mise).
* Upgraded the gRPC/Protobuf toolchain ([#391](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/391), `93c0910c`): Buf `1.65.0 → 1.75.0`, ts-proto `2.12.4 → 2.22.0`, Go gRPC `1.84.0 → 1.85.0`, `@bufbuild/protobuf` `2.11.0 → 2.17.0`, protobufjs `8.4 → 8.8`, and related validation dependencies. Regenerated TypeScript protobuf output and made proto lint cache sensitive to Buf upgrades. Later updated Go protovalidate to `1.4.1` (`a349cfe8`).
* Removed `apps/document/inquire-shim.js`, not a generated proto stub ([#392](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/392), `eabfdb45`). It had worked around protobufjs dynamic module loading in Rspack; the replacement no longer matched a dependency, and the service uses generated ts-proto package definitions instead of loading `.proto` files at runtime. The recorded investigation found byte-identical application bundles with and without the shim. See [the bundling investigation](/developer/story/nestjs-bundling-otel) and [gRPC proto-loader investigation](/developer/story/nestjs-grpc-proto-loader).
* Other notable updates include Node 26, Go 1.27.4, Nx 24.0.6, NestJS 11.2.11, TypeORM 1.1.3, Next.js 16.4.6, Vitest 5.1.1, Rspack 2.3.3, oapi-codegen 2.9.0, and OpenAPI Generator CLI 2.42.2. Infrastructure updates included PostgreSQL 18.7, Meilisearch 1.57, Grafana 13.3.1, Tempo 3, and updated Authentik, Redpanda, and RustFS images. These are selected examples, not an exhaustive dependency inventory.
* Aligned Go and Node OpenTelemetry dependencies ([#380](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/380)); pinned `cron` to `4.4.0` for compatibility with `@nestjs/schedule` (`0a59ca58`). Enabled type-aware Oxlint and fixed identified issues (`891cecbe`, `00cd90e2`).

## 5. Documentation and other improvements

* Reorganized documentation by service and topic; expanded architecture, domain, data, flow, deployment, and API pages (`cf5840a8`, `7131befe`, `5cb49a7d`). Added generated gRPC reference documentation (`12bb02cf`).
* Added validation and publication of documentation previews for pull requests (`251bab99`); fixed VitePress OpenAPI server-side rendering and documented the issue (`0df87429`, `bac0ff31`).
* Fixed document collaboration storage behavior: `flushStore` waits for queued stores, and peer modification state is preserved on load (`c11d7019`, `2273ca38`).
* Updated the workspace publication design (`fb4c5c38`, `c80f8eaa`). This is design work, not evidence that workspace publication was implemented during this period.

## 6. Future work and dependencies

### Near term

1. Finish RustFS and other homelab inputs, deploy the prepared releases, and run live security, startup, upgrade, and application-flow checks.
2. Resume prioritized billing UAT and add suitable automated integration coverage for duplicate charges, authorization, and webhook recovery. Resolve the logging and token/session security follow-up.
3. **NestJS 12:** wait for a compatible stable Nx release and confirm its Nest peer ranges before upgrading. The 2026-11-21 plan records upstream Nx support merged, but not yet available in the stable release used at that snapshot. [#350](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/350) covers the Nest upgrade; [#396](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/396) is a Terminus maintenance update, not the core blocker. The plan identified a search-worker Kafka mock requiring adaptation because Nest 12 makes `createClient` asynchronous; this was a migration finding, not a completed fix.
4. **Native ESM:** evaluate separately for document, AI, and search-worker. OpenTelemetry does not categorically prohibit ESM, but instrumentation must start before application imports and may require an ESM loader hook; Nest-specific instrumentation also has its own version-support limit. Align build output, telemetry preload, Docker and Kubernetes commands, migration/seed entrypoints, and verify actual logs, traces, startup, and shutdown. BlockNote compatibility is related but does not inherently block ESM or require an ESM application bundle. This is a plan, not an implemented migration. Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-nestjs-12-native-esm-migration.md` (`7374de9f`).
5. **TypeORM extension:** consider [#346](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/346), including CLI and fixture validation. The plan records that extension 3.9.0 has an older TypeORM peer range while the project already resolves TypeORM 1.1.3.

### Longer term

* Evaluate BlockNote `0.55 → 0.57` ([#238](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/238)), including its ESM-only distribution, server-side DOM API changes, and Yjs compatibility. Investigate whether its version-history facilities can satisfy some of the current manually saved Yjs revision and rollback requirements; compatibility and the version in which the feature first appeared have **not** been verified. Examples for future review: [Yjs 14 versioning](https://www.blocknotejs.org/examples/collaboration/versioning-yjs14) and [versioning extension](https://www.blocknotejs.org/examples/extensions/versioning). Do not assume that adopting the feature or Yjs 14 is appropriate without further investigation.

# 2026-11-24

**Kỳ báo cáo:** 25/10/2026–24/11/2026
**Commit mốc (không bao gồm):** [`69929a45c187`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/69929a45c1878d22830b3417279c631ab69a883c)
**Commit cuối trên `main` (bao gồm):** [`db8c80a424b8`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/db8c80a424b8833dc169a838e846b0c002d59ffe)

Trong kỳ này, Notopia cải thiện luồng thanh toán, hoàn thiện Helm chart và chuẩn bị triển khai trên homelab. Một số luồng thanh toán đã được kiểm thử trên Stripe sandbox; config homelab vẫn đang được hoàn thiện. Báo cáo không lặp lại phần triển khai backend AI đã trình bày kỳ trước.

## 1. Kết quả thực hiện

### 1.1. Thanh toán và gói dịch vụ

* **Mô hình nghiệp vụ:** Tổ chức lại các kiểu dữ liệu cho tiền, thanh toán, giá, đăng ký gói và hoàn tiền để làm rõ quy tắc nghiệp vụ và tránh sửa dữ liệu ngoài ý muốn. [notopia-uit/notopia#365](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/365), [dọn mã không còn dùng (`709bd76e`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/709bd76e)
* **Phát event:** Áp dụng *transactional outbox* để lưu thay đổi dữ liệu và event trong cùng một giao dịch. Luồng hủy gói và gửi yêu cầu hoàn tiền cho nhà cung cấp được xử lý bất đồng bộ qua outbox. [Commit `d78e47a3`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/d78e47a3)
* **Checkout và hoàn tiền:** Khóa theo tài khoản thanh toán của workspace khi xử lý checkout trùng; không mở lại khoản hoàn tiền đã tất toán. Đã cập nhật mã và bài kiểm thử, nhưng kịch bản checkout trùng vẫn chưa hoàn tất UAT. [Commit `d78e47a3`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/d78e47a3)
* **Tính năng và hạn mức:** Khai báo kiểu dữ liệu rõ ràng thay vì chỉ dùng khóa chuỗi chung. [Commit `f758ec9c`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/f758ec9c), [commit `18cca64c`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/18cca64c)
* **API thanh toán:** Đổi endpoint `GET /billing/workspaces/{workspaceId}/subscription` thành `GET /billing/workspaces/{workspaceId}` vì phản hồi gồm cả gói đăng ký và bên thanh toán. [Commit `a780d8bb`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/a780d8bb)
* **Cổng khách hàng Stripe:** Sửa config để nêu rõ các trường khách hàng được phép cập nhật. [Commit `5196957d`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/5196957d)

### 1.2. Kubernetes và triển khai homelab

* **Helm:** Bổ sung thư viện chart dùng chung, chart cho các dịch vụ Notopia và thành phần tiếp nhận lưu lượng có xác thực. [notopia-uit/notopia#370](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/370)
* **Chuẩn bị ứng dụng:** Tách lệnh migration và khởi tạo dữ liệu bắt buộc; bổ sung kiểm tra trạng thái sẵn sàng, bao gồm kết nối Kafka của search-worker và các phụ thuộc của Document. [Commit `72beeadf`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/72beeadf)
* **GitOps:** Chuẩn bị config Flux cho các dịch vụ, cơ sở dữ liệu, Meilisearch, Valkey và các manifest chứa secret đã mã hóa. [notopia-uit/notopia#376](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/376)
* **CI và phát hành:** Thêm kiểm tra phiên bản chart, tự động hóa phát hành và tạo bản phát hành phát triển đầu tiên. [notopia-uit/notopia#379](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/379), [commit `a97d424b`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/a97d424b)
* **Config homelab:** Bổ sung config và hướng dẫn thiết lập RustFS, webhook Stripe; một số giá trị vẫn đang được hoàn thiện. [Commit `6e9f301f`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/6e9f301f), [commit `4522f0b6`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/4522f0b6)

### 1.3. Contract API và xác thực khi phát triển

* **Schema yêu cầu:** Tách schema tạo thư mục, ghi chú và workspace khỏi schema phản hồi để máy khách không phải gửi các trường chỉ đọc do máy chủ sinh. Đây là điều chỉnh contract API, không phải nâng phiên bản OpenAPI 3.1.2. [Commit `234f7efa`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/234f7efa)
* **Xác thực:** Bổ sung tài khoản mẫu Authentik và config OAuth để thử API cục bộ. Config thử nghiệm bằng mật khẩu không dành cho production. [Authentik (`a115e9d0`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/a115e9d0), [OAuth scopes (`17cc93ac`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/17cc93ac)

### 1.4. Công cụ phát triển và chất lượng bản dựng

* **mise:** Tách config dùng chung, config cho môi trường phát triển và config cho CI; thêm lockfile theo môi trường để cài đặt công cụ nhất quán. [Commit `711a6384`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/711a6384), [commit `201943ad`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/201943ad)
* **gRPC/Protobuf:** Cập nhật Buf, ts-proto và thư viện gRPC/Protobuf; sinh lại mã TypeScript và cập nhật cách lưu bộ nhớ đệm của bước lint proto. [notopia-uit/notopia#391](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/391)
* **Đóng gói Document:** Gỡ `inquire-shim.js` vì lớp tương thích này không còn cần thiết; đối chiếu cho thấy bản đóng gói không đổi khi bỏ shim. [notopia-uit/notopia#392](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/392)
* **Telemetry và lint:** Đồng bộ các thư viện OpenTelemetry của Go và Node; bật kiểm tra kiểu với Oxlint và sửa các vấn đề được phát hiện. [notopia-uit/notopia#380](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/380), [commit `891cecbe`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/891cecbe), [commit `00cd90e2`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/00cd90e2)

### 1.5. Tài liệu

* **Cấu trúc:** Sắp xếp lại tài liệu theo dịch vụ và chủ đề, bổ sung nội dung về kiến trúc, dữ liệu và triển khai. [Commit `cf5840a8`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/cf5840a8), [commit `7131befe`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/7131befe)
* **Tham chiếu API:** Bổ sung tài liệu tham chiếu gRPC được sinh tự động và sửa lỗi hiển thị tài liệu OpenAPI khi VitePress render phía máy chủ. [gRPC (`12bb02cf`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/12bb02cf), [VitePress (`0df87429`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/0df87429)
* **Bản xem trước:** Thêm bước kiểm tra và publish bản xem trước tài liệu cho pull request. [Commit `251bab99`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/251bab99)

### 1.6. Collaboration và thiết kế publish workspace

* **Lưu tài liệu trong luồng collaboration:** Chờ các thao tác lưu trong hàng đợi hoàn tất và giữ trạng thái chỉnh sửa của người dùng khác khi tải lại tài liệu. [Commit `c11d7019`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/c11d7019), [commit `2273ca38`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/2273ca38)
* **Publish workspace:** Cập nhật thiết kế; chưa triển khai tính năng trong kỳ này. [Commit `fb4c5c38`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/fb4c5c38), [commit `c80f8eaa`](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/c80f8eaa)

## 2. Kiểm thử và tình trạng triển khai

### 2.1. Kiểm thử thanh toán

Kiểm thử thủ công bằng Scalar và Stripe sandbox ghi nhận kết quả mong đợi khi xem danh mục và quyền của workspace miễn phí, mua Plus theo tháng, hủy ngay kèm hoàn tiền, và chuyển từ Plus tháng sang Pro trọn đời. Chưa kiểm thử đầy đủ thanh toán trùng, phân quyền và khôi phục sau gián đoạn webhook. Các kết quả này không xác nhận luồng hoàn chỉnh trên giao diện hoặc mức độ sẵn sàng cho môi trường production.

[Kịch bản UAT và nhật ký tiến độ kiểm thử](https://gist.github.com/KevinNitroG/c777cd1c79d017c3ae9122fde8ebb753) được đăng trên GitHub Gist.

### 2.2. Tình trạng homelab

Đang điền secrets và biến môi trường, đồng thời hoàn thiện config cho RustFS. Hệ thống **chưa được triển khai và xác minh đầu cuối** trên homelab.

## 3. Kế hoạch theo từng giai đoạn

### 3.1. Giai đoạn tiếp theo

1. Hoàn tất config homelab và triển khai thử trên cụm Kubernetes; kiểm tra định tuyến, kiểm soát truy cập, tình trạng dịch vụ và quy trình nâng cấp.
2. Tiếp tục kiểm thử thanh toán, ưu tiên checkout trùng, phân quyền và khôi phục webhook. Sửa việc ghi dữ liệu nhạy cảm vào log và thu hồi phiên hoặc token bị ảnh hưởng.
3. **NestJS 12:** Chuẩn bị nâng cấp, nhưng chỉ thực hiện khi có bản Nx ổn định tương thích. <https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/350>
4. **Native ESM:** Đánh giá riêng việc chuyển đổi cho Document, AI và search-worker, nhất là thứ tự khởi tạo OpenTelemetry và các lệnh chạy trong container. [Kế hoạch kỹ thuật (`7374de9f`)](https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/commit/7374de9f)
5. **TypeORM extension:** Kiểm tra tương thích với TypeORM hiện tại, gồm lệnh CLI và dữ liệu mẫu. <https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/346>

### 3.2. Định hướng dài hạn

* **Nâng cấp BlockNote:** Đánh giá việc chuyển từ `0.55` lên `0.57`, gồm thay đổi về ESM, DOM phía máy chủ và khả năng tương thích với Yjs. <https://github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pull/238>
* **Demo lịch sử phiên bản:** Tham khảo [demo lưu phiên bản với Yjs 14](https://www.blocknotejs.org/examples/collaboration/versioning-yjs14) và [demo tiện ích lịch sử phiên bản](https://www.blocknotejs.org/examples/extensions/versioning) của BlockNote. Mục tiêu là xem các tính năng này có đáp ứng nhu cầu lưu và khôi phục phiên bản tài liệu của Notopia hay không. Đây là các demo tham khảo, chưa được tích hợp vào Notopia.

url: /notopia/pr/428/getting-started.md
---

# Getting Started

Local setup and the day-to-day development workflow. Everything below runs from the repo root.
For a system-wide introduction, see the [architecture overview](/architecture/overview).

## Prerequisites

Tools are managed with `mise`:

```bash
mise i            # install all tool versions
pnpm i            # install JS/TS dependencies
go mod download   # download Go dependencies
pnpm husky        # initialise hooks
```

## Infrastructure

```bash
just docker-up                    # core infrastructure (Postgres, Redis, Redpanda, Meilisearch, ...)
just docker-up-monitoring         # + Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo
compose --profile "dev-ui" up -d  # + DbGate, Redpanda Console
```

Everything is served under `*.notopia.localhost` through Traefik (`web`, `api`, `authentik`,
`traefik`, `rustfs`, `meilisearch`, `redpanda`, `dbgate`). Default credentials are
`notopiauit` / `notopiauit`.

## Run services

```bash
nx run note             # Go services run directly
nx run authorization
nx run document         # NestJS services build and watch
nx run search-worker
nx dev web              # Next.js
nx dev api-web          # Scalar API reference
```

## Code generation

API and contract changes start from the spec, never from generated code:

```bash
nx gen api     # OpenAPI: Go server, NestJS server, frontend client
nx gen proto   # Protobuf: Go, TypeScript, gRPC docs
```

## Seed vs fixtures

* **seed**: mandatory data the app needs in every environment, production included (reference
  data, default plans, the role to permission matrix). Must be idempotent. Run `just seed`.
* **fixtures**: fake data for local development only (demo workspaces, notes, memberships,
  documents, search index content). Run `just fixtures`, which runs seed first.

Per-service recipes exist as `just fixtures-note|fixtures-document|fixtures-search|...`. New
services follow the same naming: a `seed` target for mandatory data and a `fixtures` target
for dev fake data.

## Conventions

* Do not source `.env` files, Nx loads them.
* JS/TS: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsc`. Go: `golangci-lint` through `nx lint {project}`.
* Conventional commits; the pre-commit hook runs `nx affected` for typecheck, lint and format.
* Go service layout rules are in [Conventions](/developer/conventions/).

# System Architecture

Notopia is a set of small services behind a single gateway (Traefik). Go services (note,
authorization, billing) and NestJS services (document, search worker, AI) use gRPC for
synchronous service calls and Redpanda for events. The diagram shows logical dependencies;
local Compose provides infrastructure, while application services can run on the host.

Compose includes dedicated Redis instances for note, document, billing and AI. Document
Redis is optional in configuration and supports collaborative scaling and distributed locks.
Search-worker Redis is optional and not provisioned by Compose: without it, deletion
tombstones use in-memory storage suitable only for a single worker. See
[Search Worker](../services/search-worker/) for the limitations.

See [Messaging](./messaging) for the event backbone and [Auth and Gateway](./auth-and-gateway)
for how requests are authenticated.

# Messaging

Services communicate asynchronously through Redpanda (Kafka API).

## Transactional outbox

The Note and Billing services use a Watermill transactional outbox for aggregate events so
that a domain write and its outbox messages commit together. The flow in the Note service:

1. The repository `Save` drains domain events and publishes them with the Watermill
   `forwarder` publisher, which writes the message into an outbox table in the same Postgres
   transaction as the aggregate change.
2. The outbox table (default name `eventsToForward`, config `outbox_table_name`) follows the
   Watermill SQL queue schema (deleted on ack) and is created by a goose migration.
3. A Watermill SQL subscriber polls the table (every second) and the forwarder re-publishes each
   message to its real topic on Redpanda.

Authorization publishes membership events directly rather than through a transactional
outbox. NestJS services publish and consume directly with `@nestjs/microservices`; document
commit events are not atomic with the database transaction. See the
[authorization](/services/authorization/flows) and [document](/services/document/flows)
flows for delivery caveats.

## Topic naming

| Kind                          | Pattern                                            | Example                                |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Integration (cross-service)   | `events.integration.{service}.{aggregate}.{event}` | `events.integration.note.note.created` |
| Internal (inside one service) | `events.internal.{service}.*`                      | `events.internal.note.folder.renamed`  |

Every topic published or consumed by a Go service is a constant in that service's
`component/eventtopic.go`; no inline topic strings.

## Payloads

Cross-service payload types are defined once in `api/share/` (generated for Go and for
`@notopia-uit/api-share-gen`), never retyped per service. They cover document commits, note
created/updated/deleted, workspace deleted, workspace member added/removed, user workspace role
updates, user deleted and subscription changes.

See each service's page for its own topics, for example [Note events](../services/note/events).

---

---
url: /notopia/pr/428/architecture/auth-and-gateway.md
---

# Auth and Gateway

## Public traffic

All public traffic enters through Traefik, routed by path prefix on a single API host
(`/note`, `/authorization`, `/document`, `/billing`, ...). Traefik validates the Authentik JWT
with a JWT middleware, maps the OIDC `roles` claim, and injects user headers downstream. Each
service excludes its own health path from the middleware, and endpoints that must skip auth
(such as the Stripe webhook) have their own router.

* Go services read the user with `commonhttp.GatewayUserAuth()`.
* NestJS services use `UserGuard` and the `@User()` decorator.
* Exception: the `apps/document` websocket (`/document/ws/document`) validates the JWT itself.

## Internal traffic

Service-to-service calls use gRPC (definitions in `proto/`, see [protocol reference](../api/proto)).
A service never calls another service's public REST API internally. For example, Note and
Billing call the Authorization service over gRPC for permission checks, and Note calls Billing
for entitlements on every check without caching.

# Note Service

Go service owning workspaces, folders, note metadata, links, tags and trash. DDD + CQRS,
with a transactional outbox for integration events. Note only stores note metadata; the
editable binary content lives in the [Document service](../document/).

* [Domain](./domain): class diagrams
* [Data](./data): database schema
* [Flows](./flows): sequence diagrams
* [Events](./events): topics published and consumed

## Use cases

| Area              | Operations and behavior                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspaces        | Create, rename, change slug, delete, list and look up workspaces; creation also creates a root folder and owner membership.  |
| Membership        | List and update members, leave a workspace and search users. Member limits and payer protection apply to membership changes. |
| Folders and notes | Create, rename, change icons and move items; read notes and the workspace tree. Metadata is separate from document content.  |
| Trash             | Trash, restore, permanently delete or empty trash; a scheduled retention purge removes expired trash.                        |
| Discovery         | Read links and graphs, and request a workspace-scoped search token. Graphs are subject to billing entitlements.              |
| Document commits  | Consume committed content to update note size, tags and outgoing links.                                                      |

See [Flows](./flows) for authorization, billing, deletion and asynchronous event paths.
Note and workspace publishing handlers are currently stubs, not implemented publishing workflows.

## Architecture

```d2
direction: right

vars: {
  d2-config: {
    layout-engine: elk
    theme-overrides: {
      N1: "#4c4f69"
      N2: "#5c5f77"
      N4: "#acb0be"
      N5: "#ccd0da"
      N7: "#eff1f5"
      B1: "#4c4f69"
      B2: "#6c6f85"
      B3: "#bcc0cc"
      B4: "#ccd0da"
      B5: "#dce0e8"
      B6: "#eff1f5"
      AA4: "#1e66f5"
      AA5: "#7287fd"
      AB4: "#8839ef"
      AB5: "#dc8a78"
    }
  }
}

controllers: Controllers {
  http: HTTP / REST Controller
  grpc: gRPC Server
  event: Event Processor
}

application: Application {
  command_handler: Command Handler
  query_handler: Query Handler
  event_handler: Event Handler
  authorization_svc_interface: Authorization Svc Interface
  identity_svc_interface: Identity Svc Interface
  workspace_event_bus_interface: Workspace Event Bus Interface
  workspace_events: Workspace Events
  integration_event_publisher_interface: Integration Event Publisher Interface
  integration_events: Integration Events
}

domain: Domain {
  model: Domain Model
  repository_interface: Repository Interface
  domain_event: Domain Events
}

infrastructure: Infrastructure {
  persistence: Persistence/SQL
  authentik_svc: Authentication Svc

  integration_event_publisher: Integration Event Publisher
}

infrastructure -> application
infrastructure -> domain
```

```plantuml
!define Model(name) class "name" as name <<(Q, $lavender) Model>>

    TrashedBy TrashedBy

}
```

# Note Flows

The note service owns metadata; editable content and revisions belong to the [document service](../document/). These diagrams show important boundaries, not every validation or failure. For topic names and delivery details, see [Events](./events) and [Messaging](../../architecture/messaging).

## Create a workspace

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant Note as Note service
    participant DB as Note database
    participant Auth as Authorization service
    User->>Note: Create workspace (name, slug)
    Note->>DB: Begin transaction; check slug
    alt Slug already exists
        Note-->>User: Conflict
    else Available
        Note->>DB: Save workspace and root folder
        Note->>Auth: Create workspace with owner
        Auth-->>Note: Result
        Note->>DB: Commit transaction
        Note-->>User: Created
    end
```

The authorization call is made inside the database transaction, but is not part of it: a successful authorization call followed by a failed commit can leave the services inconsistent.

## Create or update a note

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant Note as Note service
    participant Auth as Authorization service
    participant DB as Note database and outbox
    participant Broker as Message broker
    participant Handler as Note event handlers
    participant SSE as Workspace SSE
    participant Search as Search worker
    User->>Note: Create note in folder
    Note->>DB: Begin transaction; find folder and workspace
    Note->>Auth: Check workspace item write permission
    alt Forbidden or folder missing
        Note-->>User: Error
    else Allowed
        Note->>DB: Save note and internal domain event
        Note->>DB: Commit
        Note-->>User: Created
        DB-->>Broker: Forward internal note.created
        Broker-->>Handler: Handle domain event
        Handler->>SSE: Publish workspace item update
        Handler->>Broker: Publish note.created integration event
        Broker-->>Search: Index note metadata
    end
```

These event handlers run asynchronously; the response does not wait for subscribers or search indexing. Updates such as rename, move, trash and restore similarly produce internal events. The integration update handler reads current note and folder state before publishing, and skips a note that no longer exists. See [Events](./events).

## Read and commit content

Note metadata is read through the note service after a workspace item permission check. The document service manages collaboration and revisions separately; see its [documentation](../document/).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant Document as Document service
    participant Broker as Message broker
    participant Note as Note service
    participant DB as Note repository
    participant Search as Search worker
    participant Index as Search index
    User->>Document: Commit document
    Document->>Document: Create revision if content changed
    Document->>Broker: Publish document.committed for new revision
    Document-->>User: Result
    Broker-->>Note: document.committed
    Note->>DB: Load note; update size, tags and outgoing links
    Note->>DB: Save note and domain events
    Broker-->>Search: document.committed
    Search->>Index: Update committed content and tags
```

The note and search consumers process the commit independently, so their updates need not be visible at the same time. A commit with no new revision does not emit this event. Automatic and scheduled commits can also trigger this path.

## Trash, restore and permanent deletion

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Trash or restore workspace items] --> B[Check workspace item delete permission]
    B --> C[Load requested items and folder descendants in transaction]
    C --> D{Operation}
    D -->|Trash| E[Mark requested items as purpose; untrashed descendants as parent]
    D -->|Restore| F[Restore requested items; restore descendants marked parent]
    E --> G[Save changed notes and folders with domain events]
    F --> G
    H[Permanent delete or empty trash] --> I[Check delete permission]
    I --> J[Load targets and affected descendant notes]
    J --> K[Delete notes through repository before folders]
    K --> L[Commit and forward internal deletion events]
    L --> M[Publish note.deleted integration event per affected note]
    M --> N[Document service removes document and revisions]
    M --> O[Search worker removes index entry]
```

Items already trashed independently remain independently trashed when their parent is trashed or restored. Permanent deletion is distinct from trashing; downstream cleanup is asynchronous.

### Automatic retention purge

The `note:purge-expired-trash` cron uses a distributed lock and runs as the service account (default 03:00 local time). It finds candidate workspaces, fetches billing entitlements in a batch, and purges explicitly trashed items older than the workspace's `trash_retention_days`, with a minimum age of 24 hours. Deleting an expired folder also deletes its descendant notes. Unlimited retention or missing entitlements skips that workspace; a billing failure skips the batch. Per-workspace failures are logged and do not stop the remaining workspaces.

## Update workspace members

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant Note as Note service
    participant Auth as Authorization service
    participant Billing as Billing service
    participant SSE as Workspace SSE
    User->>Note: Replace member list
    Note->>Note: Require nonempty list and at least one owner
    Note->>Auth: Check workspace edit permission and read current members
    Note->>Billing: Check member limit and payer protection
    alt Limit exceeded or protected payer removed/demoted
        Note-->>User: 402 or 409
    else Allowed
        Note->>Auth: Update members
        Note->>SSE: Publish members updated
        Note-->>User: Result
    end
```

The member limit blocks growth, not removals or role changes after a downgrade. A protected payer cannot be removed or demoted while billing requires one. Permission is checked before billing gates; billing unavailability returns 503. Membership update and SSE publication are separate side effects, not one transaction.

## Graphs and search

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Graph request] --> B[Check workspace item read permission]
    B --> C{Graph type}
    C -->|Workspace| D[Check workspace_graph entitlement]
    D -->|Unavailable| E[402 with required plan]
    D -->|Available| F[Read workspace graph]
    C -->|Note| G[Clamp depth to plan limit]
    G --> H[Read note graph]
    I[Workspace search token request] --> J[Check workspace read permission]
    J --> K[Generate workspace-scoped Meilisearch tenant token]
```

Billing failure returns 503 for graph queries. A note graph request above its plan's depth limit is clamped rather than rejected. Search tokens are scoped by the note service; search indexing is asynchronous.

---

---
url: /notopia/pr/428/services/note/events.md

# Note Events

Topic constants live in `internal/note/component/eventtopic.go`. See
[Messaging](../../architecture/messaging) for the outbox mechanics.

## Published: integration events

Prefix `events.integration.note.`, written through the transactional outbox.

| Topic               | Notes                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `note.created`      |                                                                                                                                 |
| `note.updated`      |                                                                                                                                 |
| `note.deleted`      | Every permanent delete (folder, note, trash) deletes the affected notes through the repo first, so each one emits its own event |
| `workspace.deleted` |                                                                                                                                 |

## Internal: domain events

Prefix `events.internal.note.`, drained from aggregates on `Save`.

| Aggregate | Topics                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| folder    | `created`, `deleted`, `renamed`, `icon_changed`, `moved`, `trashed`, `restored`, `permanently_deleted`                                                           |
| note      | `created`, `deleted`, `renamed`, `icon_changed`, `tags_changed`, `size_changed`, `moved`, `outgoing_links_changed`, `trashed`, `restored`, `permanently_deleted` |
| workspace | `renamed`, `slug_changed`, `deleted`                                                                                                                             |

A `poison` topic under the same prefix receives messages that failed handling.

## Consumed

| Topic                                             | Handler                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `events.integration.document.document.committed`  | Updates note size, tags and outgoing links                                                |
| `events.integration.billing.subscription.changed` | Publishes `WorkspaceBillingChangedEvent {workspaceId, plan}` to the workspace SSE channel |
| `events.internal.note.folder.*` and `note.*`      | Notify workspace item updates over SSE                                                    |

---
url: /notopia/pr/428/services/document.md
---

# Document Service

NestJS service holding the collaborative (Yjs / Blocknote) content of notes and serving the
realtime websocket. Note content is committed back to the Note service through events.

* [Domain](./domain): class diagrams
* [Data](./data): database schema
* [Flows](./flows): collaboration, commits, and deletion

## Use cases

| Use case                        | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Collaborate on a note           | Connect using a JWT and note read permission; users without write permission and users viewing trashed notes connect read-only. Edits are synchronized as Yjs updates and stored with a debounce.               |
| Commit content                  | A writer can commit manually. Eligible plans also commit after stores or sweep idle modified documents. A commit creates a revision and publishes content, tags, and outgoing links for downstream consumers.   |
| Manage revision history         | List revisions with pagination and an optional trigger filter, read a snapshot with content, rename it, or hard-delete it. A retention job purges old revisions according to the plan while keeping the latest. |
| Upload an attachment            | A writer requests a presigned upload URL and public URL for an attachment associated with the document.                                                                                                         |
| React to access or note changes | Workspace role and membership events update or close live connections. A note deletion closes connections and removes its document and revisions.                                                               |

HTTP authentication trusts gateway-forwarded user headers; the WebSocket validates its own JWT.
The revision handlers currently do not perform a per-document authorization check; they should not
be assumed to enforce the same permissions as commit or attachment upload.

## Architecture

```d2
direction: right

vars: {
  d2-config: {
    layout-engine: elk
    theme-overrides: {
      N1: "#4c4f69"
      N2: "#5c5f77"
      N4: "#acb0be"
      N5: "#ccd0da"
      N7: "#eff1f5"
      B1: "#4c4f69"
      B2: "#6c6f85"
      B3: "#bcc0cc"
      B4: "#ccd0da"
      B5: "#dce0e8"
      B6: "#eff1f5"
      AA4: "#1e66f5"
      AA5: "#7287fd"
      AB4: "#8839ef"
      AB5: "#dc8a78"
    }
  }
}

modules: Modules {
  api: Api (OpenAPI Generator)
  authorization: Authorization
  blocknote: Blocknote
  database: Database
  document: Document
  hocuspocus: Hocuspocus
  note: Note
  revision: Revision
  storage: Storage

  api -> document
  api -> revision
  document -> blocknote
  document -> storage
  revision -> blocknote
  revision -> authorization
  hocuspocus -> authorization
  hocuspocus -> note
}
```


```d2
vars: {

documents: {
  id: uuid {constraint: PK}

}

  contentHash: text {constraint: N}

  shape: sql_table
}

revisions.documentId -> documents.id
```

Revision content is serialized JSON stored in a text column. Revisions are hard-deleted, and
deleting a document cascades to its revisions. See [flows](./flows) for commit and deletion behavior.

# Document flows

The [Document service](./index) owns collaborative content; the Note service owns note metadata.
Stored Yjs edits are not necessarily committed revisions.

## Connect and edit

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant WS as Hocuspocus
    participant Auth as Authentication
    participant Note as Note service
    participant Permissions as Authorization service
    participant DB as Document database
    User->>WS: Connect with document ID and JWT
    WS->>Auth: Validate token
    WS->>Note: Get note for user
    WS->>Permissions: Get document permissions
    alt No read permission or note unavailable
        WS-->>User: Reject connection
    else Read allowed
        WS->>DB: Load stored Yjs state if present
        WS-->>User: Connect (read-only if no write or trashed)
        opt Writable connection
            User->>WS: Send Yjs changes
            WS->>WS: Mark modified and track contributor
            WS->>DB: Debounced store of state and modified flag
        end
    end
```

Role changes can switch a live connection between writable and read-only, or close it when read
access is lost. Membership removal closes affected connections. These updates apply to connections
observed by the event-consuming instance.

## Commit a document

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Manual["Manual commit"] --> Permission{"Write permission?"}
    Permission -- No --> Denied["Reject request"]
    Permission -- Yes --> Flush["Flush pending local store"]
    Flush --> Lock["Lock document row in transaction"]
    Store["After document store"] --> Auto{"Auto-commit enabled and due?"}
    Auto -- Yes --> Lock
    Auto -- No --> Skip["Skip"]
    Sweep["Sweep idle modified documents"] --> Eligible{"Plan enables auto-commit?"}
    Eligible -- Yes --> Lock
    Eligible -- No --> Skip
    Lock --> Due{"Modified and due?"}
    Due -- No --> NoChange["No new revision"]
    Due -- Yes --> Hash{"Content matches latest revision?"}
    Hash -- Yes --> Clear["Clear stored modified flag"]
    Hash -- No --> Revision["Save revision, clear modified and contributors"]
    Revision --> Event["Emit document committed event"]
    Clear --> Memory["Clear loaded modified flag only if content hash still matches"]
    Event --> Memory
    Event --> Note["Note: update size, tags and links"]
    Event --> Search["Search worker: index committed content"]
```

Manual commit bypasses the interval gate but still requires modified content. It returns `201` with
the new revision ID, `200` with the latest ID when no new revision is created, or `204` if there is
no revision. Hash-equivalent content clears the stored modified flag without creating a revision;
pending contributors are retained for the next actual commit. Comparing the loaded content hash
before clearing its flag protects newer, not-yet-stored edits, including delete-only edits.

Auto-commit checks the workspace plan and its minimum interval; the sweeper forces commits of idle
modified documents only for plans with auto-commit enabled. When billing is unavailable these
background paths skip work rather than prevent editing. The Kafka emit occurs inside the database
transaction, but it is not a transactional outbox: database and event delivery are not atomic.
Search and note metadata reflect committed content, not every collaborative edit.

## Delete a note

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Note as Note service
    participant Events as Kafka
    participant WS as Hocuspocus instance
    participant DB as Document database
    Note->>Events: Publish note deleted
    Events->>WS: Deliver deletion event
    WS->>WS: Guard loaded document against further stores
    WS->>WS: Close connections and wait for in-flight stores
    WS->>DB: Delete document
    DB->>DB: Cascade delete revisions
```

The guard prevents a final unload store from recreating a deleted document on the receiving
instance. In a scaled deployment, deletion must reach every instance holding that document; the
local guard alone does not provide cross-instance delivery.

url: /notopia/pr/428/services/authorization.md
---

# Authorization Service

Go service that answers permission checks (Casbin policies, workspace memberships and roles)
over gRPC for the other services.

* [Domain](./domain): class diagrams
* [Data](./data): database schema
* [Flows](./flows): permission checks and membership changes

## Use cases

Authorization exposes an internal gRPC API; callers supply the user and workspace IDs.
It stores workspace-scoped role assignments, not workspace metadata or individual note
ACLs. The calling service is responsible for identifying the user and enforcing the
result of a check.

| Use case                  | RPC                                                    | Behavior                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create initial membership | `CreateWorkspaceWithOwner`                             | Adds the supplied owner-to-workspace role assignment; a duplicate assignment is an error.                                                 |
| List a user's workspaces  | `GetUserWorkspaces`                                    | Returns workspace IDs and roles from that user's grouping policies.                                                                       |
| List members              | `GetWorkspaceMembers`                                  | Requires workspace read permission and returns user IDs and roles.                                                                        |
| Replace members           | `UpdateWorkspaceMembers`                               | Requires workspace edit permission and replaces the complete membership list, generating events for additions, role changes and removals. |
| Leave a workspace         | `LeaveWorkspace`                                       | Removes the caller's membership, except when the caller is the only owner.                                                                |
| Delete authorization data | `DeleteWorkspace`                                      | Requires workspace delete permission and removes all membership policies for that workspace, not the workspace itself.                    |
| Check access              | `HasWorkspacePermission`, `HasWorkspaceItemPermission` | Return a boolean for a workspace action or a workspace-wide item action.                                                                  |
| Get item capabilities     | `GetUserWorkspaceItemPermissions`                      | Requires workspace read permission, then returns item read, write and delete decisions.                                                   |

The replacement request must contain at least one member. Unlike `LeaveWorkspace`, its
handler does not check that an owner remains. These operations do not create or delete
the corresponding workspace in another service.

## Roles and permissions

The seeded policy grants the following actions:

| Role   | Workspace                                        | Workspace items     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| Owner  | read, edit, delete, billing read, billing manage | read, write, delete |
| Editor | read, billing read                               | read, write, delete |
| Viewer | read, billing read                               | read                |

Casbin's `g` policies associate a user with a role in a workspace. Static `p` policies
grant actions to roles; `g2` maps note and folder objects to the `workspace_item` class.
The item-check RPCs check the class for the whole workspace, not a particular item ID.

The static policy is seeded separately with `just seed-authorization`; development
memberships are loaded separately with `just fixtures-authorization`. At startup,
policy drift is logged and fails the policy health check; the running enforcer does not
watch the database, so restart it after correcting the seed.

## Architecture

```d2
direction: right

vars: {
  d2-config: {
    layout-engine: elk
    theme-overrides: {
      N1: "#4c4f69"
      N2: "#5c5f77"
      N4: "#acb0be"
      N5: "#ccd0da"
      N7: "#eff1f5"
      B1: "#4c4f69"
      B2: "#6c6f85"
      B3: "#bcc0cc"
      B4: "#ccd0da"
      B5: "#dce0e8"
      B6: "#eff1f5"
      AA4: "#1e66f5"
      AA5: "#7287fd"
      AB4: "#8839ef"
      AB5: "#dc8a78"
    }
  }
}

controllers: Controllers {
  grpc: gRPC
}

application: Application

infrastructure: Infrastructure {
  casbin_enforcer: Casbin Enforcer
  persistence: Persistence/GORM
}

controllers -> application
application -> infrastructure
```

# Authorization Flows

These flows describe the internal gRPC service. See the [overview](./index) for the
complete use-case and role-permission summaries.

## Check a permission

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Calling service
    participant Auth as Authorization gRPC
    participant Casbin
    Caller->>Auth: HasWorkspacePermission or HasWorkspaceItemPermission
    Auth->>Casbin: Enforce(user, workspace, object class, action)
    Note over Casbin: Match workspace-scoped role and role policy
    Casbin-->>Auth: allow or deny
    Auth-->>Caller: has_permission
```

An enforcement error is returned as an error rather than a denial. For the combined
`GetUserWorkspaceItemPermissions` query, the service first requires workspace read,
then batch-checks item read, write and delete. Unlike the single permission checks,
the combined query returns an error when workspace read is denied.

## Replace workspace members

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Calling service
    participant Auth as Authorization gRPC
    participant Casbin
    participant Kafka as Kafka publisher
    Caller->>Auth: UpdateWorkspaceMembers(user, workspace, complete list)
    Auth->>Casbin: Enforce workspace edit
    alt denied
        Casbin-->>Auth: deny
        Auth-->>Caller: permission error
    else allowed
        Casbin-->>Auth: allow
        Auth->>Casbin: Begin transaction and read current memberships
        Auth->>Casbin: Replace grouping policies
        Note over Auth: Compare old and new members
        opt membership changes
            Auth->>Kafka: Publish added, role-updated and removed events
        end
        Auth->>Casbin: Complete transaction
        Auth-->>Caller: success
    end
```

Publishing happens inside the Casbin transaction callback, through a direct Kafka
publisher, not a transactional outbox. Events are published individually, so partial
publication is possible and delivery is not atomic with the membership transaction.
On a publishing error the callback returns an error, but the update gRPC handler logs
that specific error and returns success. Do not interpret that response as a guarantee
that either all events were delivered or the membership transaction committed.

## Leave a workspace

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[LeaveWorkspace] --> B[Read workspace memberships in transaction]
    B --> C{User is a member?}
    C -- No --> D[Return permission error]
    C -- Yes --> E{User is the only owner?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Return only-owner error]
    E -- No --> G[Remove user grouping policy]
    G --> H[Publish member-removed event]
    H --> I{Publish succeeded?}
    I -- Yes --> J[Complete transaction and return success]
    I -- No --> K[Return error from transaction]
```

Unlike member replacement, leave propagates a publication error to the caller. The
direct publication is still not atomic with the Casbin transaction.

## Delete workspace authorization

`DeleteWorkspace` checks workspace delete permission before removing all grouping
policies for the workspace. It does not publish member-removal events in this handler;
workspace deletion and any related cleanup belong to the calling workflow.

url: /notopia/pr/428/services/billing.md

# Billing Service

Plans, prices, subscriptions and entitlements. Stripe (sandbox) through hosted Checkout and
Customer Portal. DDD + CQRS like the Note service, with a Watermill transactional outbox:
domain writes and event publishes commit together. Other services read entitlements
over gRPC and never cache them.

* [Domain](./domain): class diagrams
* [Data](./data): database diagram
* [Flows](./flows): checkout and portal, entitlements, webhooks, cancellation, payer changes and crons

## Use cases

| Actor                           | Use case                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace member                | View available plans and prices; read workspace entitlements with `billing_read`.                                                                                                                                                              |
| Billing manager                 | View the workspace subscription and payer, [start checkout](./flows#checkout), open the [customer portal](./flows#customer-portal), preview or request [cancel-now](./flows#cancel-now), and [claim payer](./flows#payer-removed-and-claimed). |
| Internal service                | Resolve one or many workspace [entitlements](./flows#entitlement-resolution) over gRPC.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Administrator                   | List and update plans, read or update billing policy, and create or archive prices.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Stripe and background workers   | [Synchronize webhooks](./flows#webhook-pipeline), process outbox side effects and reconcile stale or pending work.                                                                                                                             |
| Note and Authorization services | Trigger cancellation on [workspace deletion](./flows#workspace-deletion) or handle [payer removal](./flows#payer-removed-and-claimed).                                                                                                         |

## Plan features and limits

The HTTP API exposes the known feature flags `auto_commit` and `workspace_graph`, and limits
`members`, `published_notes`, `note_graph_max_depth`, `auto_commit_min_interval_seconds`,
`revision_history_days`, `trash_retention_days`, and `ai_credits_monthly`. Limits are integers
of at least `-1`; `-1` means unlimited. Plan updates are partial: omitted keys remain unchanged.
Unknown keys are rejected.

The billing gRPC API uses typed `Features` and `Limits` messages with optional scalar fields,
so an absent value remains distinguishable from `false` or `0`. The change from string-keyed
maps uses new protobuf field numbers: billing and its note, document, and AI consumers must be
deployed together. Mixed versions do not exchange features or limits correctly.

## Architecture

```d2
direction: right

vars: {
  d2-config: {
    layout-engine: elk
    theme-overrides: {
      N1: "#4c4f69"
      N2: "#5c5f77"
      N4: "#acb0be"
      N5: "#ccd0da"
      N7: "#eff1f5"
      B1: "#4c4f69"
      B2: "#6c6f85"
      B3: "#bcc0cc"
      B4: "#ccd0da"
      B5: "#dce0e8"
      B6: "#eff1f5"
      AA4: "#1e66f5"
      AA5: "#7287fd"
      AB4: "#8839ef"
      AB5: "#dc8a78"
    }
  }
}

controllers: Controllers {
  http: HTTP (gin strict) {
    api: Workspace + admin APIs
    webhook: Stripe webhook
  }
  grpc: gRPC (entitlements)
  event: Kafka consumers
  cron: Crons (Redis-locked)
}

application: Application {
  cmds: Commands
  queries: Queries
}

domain: Domain {
  subscription: Subscription + Refund
  account: BillingAccount
  catalog: Price / Plan / BillingPolicy
}

infrastructure: Infrastructure {
  persistence: Postgres (sqlc)
  stripe: Stripe adapter
  outbox: Outbox (Watermill, outbox_messages)
  authorization: Authorization gRPC client
  redis: Redis (cron locks)
}

stripe_cloud: Stripe {shape: cloud}
kafka: Redpanda {shape: queue}
authz: Authorization Service
note: Note Service

controllers -> application
application -> domain
application -> infrastructure
infrastructure.stripe -> stripe_cloud
stripe_cloud -> controllers.http.webhook: webhook events
infrastructure.persistence -> infrastructure.outbox: events in the same tx
infrastructure.outbox -> kafka: forwarder
kafka -> controllers.event: workspace.deleted\nrole_updated\nmember_removed\nsubscription.canceled_now\nsubscription.refund_requested
infrastructure.authorization -> authz
note -> controllers.grpc: entitlement checks
```

## Events

Repo `Save` writes the aggregate's popped domain events into `outbox_messages` in the same
transaction. `outbox.Forwarder` relays them to Kafka, keyed by the aggregate id (workspace id
for the integration event). Topics are declared once in `internal/billing/component/eventtopic.go`.

### Published

| Topic                                             | Payload                       | When                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `events.integration.billing.subscription.changed` | `{workspaceId, plan, status}` | `SubscriptionStateChangedEvent`: recorded whenever a subscription's plan or status changes (not for duplicate checkouts)                                      |
| `events.internal.billing.{aggregate}.{event}`     | the domain event              | every other domain event, e.g. `subscription.canceled_now`, `subscription.refund_requested`, `billing_account.payer_missing`, `price.created`, `plan.updated` |

The `events.internal.*` topics are billing's own: only billing consumes them (see below).

### Consumed

| Topic                                                          | Use case                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `events.integration.note.workspace.deleted`                    | `HandleWorkspaceDeleted`                              |
| `events.integration.authorization.user_workspace_role_updated` | `HandlePayerRemoved` (payer no longer owner)          |
| `events.integration.authorization.workspace_member_removed`    | `HandlePayerRemoved`                                  |
| `events.internal.billing.subscription.canceled_now`            | `CancelProviderSubscription` (cancel at the provider) |
| `events.internal.billing.subscription.refund_requested`        | `SubmitRefund` (create the provider refund)           |

One consumer group per topic. An undecodable payload or a permanent error (`notFound`, `invalid`) is logged and acked; other errors are retried.

url: /notopia/pr/428/services/billing/domain.md

# Billing Class Diagram

:::info

* Golang syntax
* Apply DDD, CQRS, repository pattern, clean architecture
* Derived from `internal/billing/domain` and `internal/billing/app`

:::

## Domain Layer

`BillingAccount` owns the payer's recorded contact details; `Subscription` owns its
refunds and references a catalog `Price`. The subscription's plan and interval are the
purchased terms. Provider snapshots describe Stripe state, and payment coverage belongs
to each payment, not the subscription's current period. A refund keeps its payment
reference and amount after the temporary quote is gone.

```plantuml
PlanRepo -- Plan
BillingPolicyRepo -- BillingPolicy
@enduml
```

## Application Layer

`CancelNow` only records the local cancellation and refund requests. The provider side effects are separate commands driven by billing's own outbox events (see [Flows](./flows#cancel-now)).

# Billing Database Diagram

:::info

* Only column marked with `N` mean nullable
* The Watermill outbox table (`outbox_messages`) is omitted
* `workspace_id` is a logical reference to the Note service workspace (no cross-service FK)

:::

```d2
vars: {
```

# Billing Flows

:::info

* Stripe runs in **sandbox** only: Stripe doesn't onboard Vietnamese businesses for live payouts. See [the payment provider story](/developer/story/BILLING_PAYMENT_PROVIDERS).
* Webhook handlers extract object IDs from the payload and fetch current state from Stripe instead of applying the payload as a snapshot.
* Entitlements are always read from billing's own database. Other services call gRPC on every check and never cache.

:::

## Subscription States

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> incomplete: checkout created subscription
  incomplete --> active: first invoice paid
  incomplete --> incomplete_expired: not paid in 23h
  active --> past_due: renewal payment failed
  past_due --> active: retry succeeded
  past_due --> unpaid: retries exhausted
  active --> canceled: period end or cancel-now
  past_due --> canceled
  unpaid --> canceled
```

This is a simplified recurring-provider lifecycle, not an exhaustive transition graph. `past_due` keeps paid features until period end + `pastDueGraceDays` (billing policy, default 3). Lifetime purchases have no Stripe subscription: they're created `active` and can be canceled by the user within the refund window or on workspace deletion.

## Checkout

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber

    actor U as Owner
    participant B as Billing
    participant AS as Authorization Service
    participant S as Stripe

    U->>+B: POST /billing/workspaces/{id}/checkout-session {priceId}
    B->>+AS: HasWorkspacePermission(billing_manage)
    AS-->>-B: Ok
    B->>B: Check active price and current subscription
    opt No billing account yet
        B->>S: Create customer (idempotency key customer:{workspaceId})
        B->>B: Save BillingAccount
    end
    B->>S: Create Checkout Session (metadata: workspace, price, purpose)
    B-->>-U: { url }
    U->>S: Pay on checkout.stripe.com
    S-->>U: Redirect to workspace billing settings
    S->>B: checkout.session.completed webhook
    B->>S: Fetch completed session and provider state
    B->>B: Commit subscription and outbox events
```

Checkout rejects archived prices and existing subscriptions, except a lifetime purchase replacing a
recurring subscription. The redirect itself does not update billing state. On webhook completion,
the billing account is locked to serialize concurrent checkouts:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Completed checkout] --> B{Purchase type}
    B -->|Recurring| C{Current subscription?}
    C -->|No| D[Create subscription and set payer]
    C -->|Yes| E[Record duplicate for cancellation and refund]
    B -->|Lifetime| F{Current subscription?}
    F -->|None| G[Create lifetime subscription and set payer]
    F -->|Recurring| H[Cancel locally and request unused-time refunds]
    H --> G
    F -->|Lifetime| E
    E --> I[Outbox drives provider cancellation and refunds]
    H --> I
```

If the recurring subscription changes between fetching its payments and locking it for replacement,
the transaction fails and webhook delivery can be retried.

## Customer Portal

A user with `billing_manage` can start a portal session for an existing billing account. Billing
requires a seeded portal configuration and returns a Stripe-hosted URL. Plan changes and
period-end cancellation made there reach the local subscription through subscription or invoice
webhooks; the return URL is not itself a synchronization operation. See
[Webhook Pipeline](#webhook-pipeline).

## Entitlement Resolution

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Entitlement request] --> B[Read current subscription, plans and policy]
    B --> C{Subscription grants access now?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Return purchased tier features and limits]
    C -->|No| E[Return free tier features and limits]
    D --> F[Include subscription status and access-until]
    E --> G[Include current status, or none when absent]
```

HTTP requests check `billing_read`; internal consumers use the single or batch gRPC API. Resolution
uses the local database, not a synchronous Stripe request. A subscription may retain its status in
the response even when the free tier applies.

## Webhook Pipeline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber

    participant S as Stripe
    participant B as Billing
    participant DB as Billing DB
    participant K as Kafka

    S->>+B: POST /billing/webhooks/stripe (signed)
    B->>B: Verify signature on the raw body
    B->>S: Fetch checkout session / subscription / refund
    B->>DB: tx: MarkProcessed(event.id) + apply local state
    Note over B,DB: Duplicate event ID does not apply state again

    Note over B,DB: Save also writes the aggregate's events to outbox_messages (same tx)
    B-->>-S: 204

    DB--)K: Outbox forwarder publishes events asynchronously
    K--)B: Internal canceled_now / refund_requested events
    opt Locally canceled recurring subscription
        B->>S: Cancel provider subscription (idempotent), then MarkProviderSynced
    end
    opt Refund due
        B->>S: Create refund (idempotency key refund:{id})
        B->>DB: Save provider refund id + status
    end
```

Processing details:

1. Provider reads and idempotent mutations that must not be lost (change the default card) run **before** the write transaction. Checkout completion locks the workspace's billing account inside the transaction and decides duplicate / replace there, so concurrent checkouts of one workspace serialize.
2. For handled objects, the write transaction records the event (`processed_provider_events`) together with the state change and the outbox events. An unknown subscription can be acknowledged before checkout creates it; checkout fetches its own current snapshot. Unhandled event types are acknowledged and ignored.
3. **Phase 2** is driven by billing's own outbox events, consumed in `controller/event`: `subscription.canceled_now` runs `CancelProviderSubscription` (cancel at the provider, then `MarkProviderSynced`), and `subscription.refund_requested` runs `SubmitRefund` (`CreateRefund` keyed by the refund id; a provider `invalid` error marks the refund `failed`). A locally canceled row is never resurrected.
4. The hourly reconcile cron is the safety net: it retries provider cancels and refund submissions for rows still awaiting them.

## Cancel Now

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber

    actor U as Owner
    participant B as Billing
    participant S as Stripe
    participant DB as Billing DB

    U->>+B: GET .../subscription/cancel-now/preview
    B->>S: Period payments (recurring) / payment intent (lifetime)
    B-->>-U: Refund quote
    U->>+B: POST .../subscription/cancel-now
    B->>DB: tx: Subscription canceled + any pending refunds + outbox events
    B-->>-U: Workspace billing (subscription: null)
    opt Recurring subscription
        DB--)B: outbox: subscription.canceled_now
        B->>S: Cancel subscription now, then MarkProviderSynced
    end
    opt Positive refund lines
        DB--)B: outbox: subscription.refund_requested
        B->>S: Create refund (refund:{id})
        B->>DB: Save provider refund ID and status
        S->>B: Refund webhook; fetch and sync status
    end
```

Recurring refunds are prorated per payment's own coverage window, capped by the amount not already
refunded. Lifetime purchases are refundable within the policy window; after it expires user
cancel-now is rejected. Preview is not a reservation: cancel-now fetches payments and calculates a
fresh quote. Refunds can remain pending, succeed, fail, or be canceled.

### Workspace deletion

The Note service's workspace-deleted event invokes the same local cancellation and asynchronous
provider/refund pipeline. If no current subscription exists it is a no-op. A lifetime subscription
outside its refund window is still canceled, but without a refund.

## Payer Removed and Claimed

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber

    participant AS as Authorization Service
    participant K as Kafka
    participant B as Billing
    participant S as Stripe
    actor O as Another Owner

    AS--)K: user_workspace_role_updated / workspace_member_removed
    K--)B: Payer lost the owner role
    opt Current recurring subscription
        B->>S: Schedule cancellation at period end
    end
    B->>S: Detach payment methods
    B->>B: Mark payer missing and schedule local cancellation if recurring
    O->>+B: POST .../payer/claim
    B-->>-O: Setup-mode checkout URL
    O->>S: Save a card
    S->>B: checkout.session.completed (payer_change)
    B->>S: Set default card, detach others, update contact
    opt Payer was missing and recurring cancellation scheduled
        B->>S: Resume subscription
    end
    B->>B: Record payer and any resumed subscription
```

Claiming requires `billing_manage` and an existing billing account; it is also available when the
previous payer is not missing, provided the caller is not already the recorded payer. Only events
affecting the recorded payer trigger removal handling.

## Crons

| Job                               | Schedule                   | Effect                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `billing:reconcile-subscriptions` | hourly                     | Re-syncs subscriptions past their period end or not synced for 24 h; retries provider cancels and refund submissions still pending |
| `billing:prune-provider-events`   | daily 04:00 (process `TZ`) | Deletes processed webhook event ids older than 30 days                                                                             |

Both use a Redis lock (`billing_redis`), so with several billing instances each tick runs once.
